rows.grounds: those from whom it must be hidden

items.question: From whom must this Kaula teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed.
Concealment requires deliberate effort.
The lowest of men in the mortal world are the ones from whom it must be hidden.
items.inference: This teaching must be kept secret with effort from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: Under what condition may this teaching be given to a recipient?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
The giving is connected with one previously accomplished.
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to one who has been tested for a year in relation to the previously accomplished.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic role of pūrvasiddhasya is slightly ambiguous.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who has been tested for one year by the previously accomplished.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The section is numbered fifth.
The section is called a chapter.
items.inference: This marks the end of the fifth chapter in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known to the speaker?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge.
The knowledge concerns the determination of Kaula.
The cause of this knowledge is the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.inference: The speaker has come to know the Kaula determination through the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the true identity and essential nature of the soul that has been declared?
premises: The soul has been declared in the teaching.
Its identity is asked about.
Its essential nature is asked about as an alternative formulation.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both who the declared soul is and what its essential nature is.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation of this process is requested?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution.
The locus of that dissolution is questioned.
The speaker asks for a complete explanation.
items.inference: The teaching must explain where the soul dissolves and clarify all related matters.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme and unconditioned qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme.
It is partless and eternal.
It is free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The reality in question is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and free from all defect and stain.
uncertainties: The referent of saḥ may be the soul or the supreme principle depending on context.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa, power, and individuality?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That same soul is identified as haṃsa.
It is also characterized as power and individual.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, possessing the nature of power and individuality.
uncertainties: The compound śakti+pudgalaḥ can be read in more than one doctrinal sense.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filled vital air abide within all living beings?
premises: There is a breath-filled air.
This air is situated in all beings.
Its presence is universal among living beings.
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the transmitted form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What identity is ascribed to the soul immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The subject leaves the body.
This leaving is described as merely occurring.
At that point the subject is called supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that being is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as he leaves the body, he is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching received and transmitted according to traditional lineage?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear.
It comes down through a sequence of tradition.
The goddess is addressed as the recipient of this statement.
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through an unbroken tradition.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What transformative power is attributed to merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone.
The knowledge is received by hearing.
The statement is addressed to the fair-faced one.
items.inference: Mere hearing of this knowledge is presented as having significant effect.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically incomplete and its main result is carried into the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, heard and received...

rows.grounds: object or state associated with practice

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: One should practice for six months.
The practice is undertaken by a qualified person.
The result is described as free from bondage.
items.inference: Six months of this practice leads to a condition free from bondage.
uncertainties: The role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous in this context.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months attains the ochre state, free from bondage.

items.question: What benefits of health and spiritual companionship result from this practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
The practitioner gains association with yogis.
These outcomes follow the prescribed practice.
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What instruction regarding the practice concerning the soul has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: The teaching concerns the practice of the soul.
It has been told to the listener.
Bhairavī is explicitly addressed.
items.inference: The instruction on the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To what kind of resolved and fully prepared person may this teaching be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is endowed with all states.
The recipient has a firmly resolved mind.
items.inference: This teaching may be given to one who is fully prepared and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The case forms suggest a compressed construction with some syntactic ambiguity.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and of resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified.
It originates from the yoginīs.
It is explicitly declared not to be given.
items.inference: The essential Kaula teaching arising from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to the rest of the clause is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation from ignorance to purity is claimed for the speaker's body now?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance.
The speaker refers to the present moment.
The body is now described as pure.
items.inference: The speaker claims that the body, once veiled by ignorance, is now pure.
uncertainties: The case ending of deham is unexpected for a nominative subject in this form.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming the power of time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear.
The topic is the deception or overcoming of time.
This teaching is described as auspicious.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means for overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given that death can be destroyed through the teaching to be explained?
premises: The teacher promises to explain.
There is said to be no doubt.
The explanation shows how death is destroyed.
items.inference: The teaching will certainly explain how death is destroyed.
items.plain_english: I will tell you; there is no doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected by the burning force at the tip of nectar?
premises: There is a burning at the tip of nectar.
This occurs through the essence of juice.
Even a wise person is affected.
items.inference: Even the wise can be burned by the force associated with the tip of nectar and its essence.
uncertainties: The physiological and doctrinal referents of amṛta+agraṃ and rasa+agreṇa are not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Even the wise person is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath at the root of tongue and palate should be performed slowly?
premises: The practice is located at the root of the tongue and palate.
The practitioner acts upon the breath.
The breath should be drunk slowly.
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Having fixed it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath technique continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year.
The practice becomes well established.
Old age and death are destroyed as a result.
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to poison is attained in the body even after bites from great serpents?
premises: The body may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison would normally enter the body.
In this case poison does not enter.
items.inference: Through this attainment, poison does not enter the body even when bitten by great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
